analysis.title: Walmart Inc. (WMT): Share gains continued across categories, supported by price investment; FY26 guidance raised
key_insights: Walmart closed down 1.0% (vs. S&P 500 at -2.0%) after a 3Q earnings beat and a raise to 2026 guidance at the midpoint.
Walmart US comp sales were +2.9%, in line with consensus (FactSet), up from +2.6% in 2Q. Traffic was +1.5% and average ticket +1.4%, including a ~70 bps net headwind from pharmacy deflation.

Price investments produced share gains, particularly in grocery, where Walmart saw some of its highest share gains in three years. Walmart US grocery comps were up mid-single digits, and like-for-like grocery inflation was +1.4%, including a -40 bps impact from egg deflation.
eCommerce sales rose 23%, with nearly 50% growth in marketplace sales. Walmart US general merchandise GMV grew mid-single digits, above the low-single-digit reported comp for the category.
3Q operating income was $7,770mn, a 4.1% margin versus consensus of 4.0%. Global operating income (cc) grew 5.5% y/y, above the 3Q guide of +2.0-4.0% and ahead of net sales (cc) at +4.4%.
2026 net sales growth (cc) guidance is now +4.9-5.2%, up from +4.0-5.0% (vs. consensus of +5.6%). This implies 4Q net sales growth (cc) of +4.5-5.5% (vs. consensus of +5.0%).

2026 adj. operating income growth (cc) guidance is now +8.0-8.6%, up from +7.0-8.5%. Adj. EPS guidance is $2.84-2.89, up from $2.80-2.87 (vs. consensus of $2.89). The 4Q implied adj. EPS is $0.73-0.78 (vs. consensus of $0.78).

Maximum Fair Pricing (MFP) is expected to be a ~125 bp headwind to the Walmart US comp, partly offset by a ~50 bps GLP-1 tailwind (unchanged from the prior guide). The timing of Flipkart's BBD event should add ~100 bps to 4Q sales growth.

Management expects a strong holiday season. Back-to-school and Halloween both went well, and Walmart treats back-to-school as an early indicator of holiday performance. Marketplace inventory has been forward-deployed into a couple hundred stores.

Walmart US had ~7.7K rollbacks at the end of 3Q, above the ~5.0-5.5K average and returning toward historical levels. Management plans to keep prices as low as possible for as long as possible, while noting cost pressure in fuel and transportation.
GS sees a degree of conservatism in the 2026 guidance given macro uncertainty, and expects Walmart to keep benefiting from share gains for the rest of the year.

GS reiterates Buy and raises the 12-month price target to $134 from $132. The target rests on downside/base/upside relative P/E multiples of 210%/215%/220% (vs. 160%/165%/170% prior) and a lower market multiple of 17.3x (vs. 22.8x prior).

GS estimate changes: 2026 revenue growth +5.9% (from +5.6%), 2026 gross margin 24.6% (from 24.5%), 2026 EPS $2.91 (from $2.90), 2027 EPS $3.19 (from $3.21), 2028 EPS $3.65 (from $3.66). The 4Q26 EPS estimate is unchanged at $0.79, and a new 2029 EPS estimate of $4.16 is introduced.

market_movers.rationale: GS reiterates Buy and raises the target to $134 from $132 after the 3Q beat and guidance raise. It cites continued share gains from price investment and conservatism in the 2026 guide.

sector_views.rationale: Walmart is gaining share in grocery and other categories on value and convenience, and GS expects its profitability to keep improving.

earnings_insights: 3Q (reported 11/19): Walmart US comp +2.9% vs consensus +2.9% (FactSet), accelerating from +2.6% in 2Q.
3Q operating income was $7,770mn (reported), a 4.1% margin vs consensus of 4.0%. Global operating income (cc) grew +5.5% y/y vs the 3Q guide of +2.0-4.0%.

2026 guidance (company, raised): adj. EPS $2.84-2.89 (prior $2.80-2.87; consensus $2.89), net sales growth (cc) +4.9-5.2% (prior +4.0-5.0%; consensus +5.6%), adj. operating income growth (cc) +8.0-8.6% (prior +7.0-8.5%).
4Q implied by guidance: adj. EPS $0.73-0.78 (consensus $0.78), net sales growth (cc) +4.5-5.5% (consensus +5.0%), adj. operating income growth (cc) +4.0-6.0%.
GS estimates (not reported figures): 4Q26 adj. EPS $0.79 (unchanged), FY26 adj. EPS $2.91, 2027 EPS $3.19, 2028 EPS $3.65, 2029 EPS $4.16.
risk_factors: Inability to use expense leverage to offset investments in e-commerce and pricing.
Pressure from wages or transportation costs, including fuel.
MFP headwind of ~125 bp to the Walmart US comp.
